chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated allelic effect at rs6983267
predictions: There is no allele-specific TF occupancy at rs6983267 that changes enhancer activity in colorectal cells.
The colorectal cancer association is explained by a linked causal variant, a passenger event, or another non-TF mechanism at 8q24.
QBiC-SELEX binding differences at the site do not translate into a functional allele-specific effect in the relevant cell type.

chains.title: NR2F6 binds the alt T allele at the 8q24 pELS and activates POU5F1B in colorectal cells

links.claim: NR2F6 has its own QBiC-SELEX model in group G002 (best model z 20.82, effect +1.92), predicting that the alt T allele binds NR2F6 more strongly; NR2F6 is expressed at 37.02 TPM in the supplied HCT116 context. This is an in vitro binding prediction, not allele-specific ChIP evidence.
rs6983267 lies in the proximal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3858447 with DNase and H3K27ac signal consistent with an active enhancer.

POU5F1B is the nearest protein-coding gene, has the strongest supplied L2G score, is a TWAS candidate with CRC growth/metastasis literature support, and the alt T allele is associated with higher POU5F1B expression in Colon-Transverse (NES +0.20); direct enhancer-POU5F1B contact is not shown.
NR2F6 is expressed at 37.02 TPM in the supplied HCT116 colorectal cancer expression context, supporting this cell type as a relevant test system.

The variant is strongly associated with colorectal cancer at 8q24.21; the strongest CRC GWAS row lists effect allele T, and the alt T allele is associated with higher POU5F1B in colon transverse, but effect alleles across colon phenotypes are mixed.

predictions: The alt T allele shows stronger NR2F6 binding than the ref G allele at rs6983267.
NR2F6 occupies the EH38E3858447 enhancer in colorectal cells and NR2F6 perturbation changes POU5F1B expression.
An allele-specific enhancer reporter shows higher alt-T activity in an NR2F6-dependent manner.
falsified_if: NR2F6 does not bind the variant allele-specifically in colorectal cells.
The alt T allele does not increase NR2F6 occupancy or NR2F6-dependent enhancer activity.
NR2F6 perturbation does not change POU5F1B expression or the enhancer reporter.

chains.title: TCF7L2 occupies the 8q24 pELS in HCT116; proposed ref-G binding and MYC regulation

links.claim: An ENCODE TCF7L2 ChIP-seq peak in HCT116 contains chr8:127401060:G>T, supporting TCF7L2 occupancy at the element, but this does not establish allele specificity. The chain proposes that the ref G allele binds TCF7L2 more strongly; no TCF7L2 QBiC-SELEX row or qbic_tf_detail lookup is supplied, so QBiC coverage is not_checked and no QBiC direction is claimed.
rs6983267 lies in the proximal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3858447 with DNase and H3K27ac signal consistent with an active enhancer.
MYC lies about 334 kb upstream and is a plausible 8q24 target, but no 3D contact, reporter, CRISPR, or allele-specific assay links this enhancer to MYC.

HCT116 is the supplied DepMap expression context and has a TCF7L2 ChIP-seq peak containing the variant, supporting HCT116 as a relevant colorectal model, though TCF7L2 expression is not quantified in the supplied evidence.

The variant is strongly associated with colorectal cancer at 8q24.21, but the strongest CRC row lists effect allele T whereas some colon rows list G, creating direction tension with a ref-G TCF7L2-binding/MYC-raising model.

predictions: TCF7L2 occupies chr8:127401060 in HCT116, consistent with the ENCODE peak.
If allele-specific, the ref G allele shows stronger TCF7L2 binding than the alt T allele.
TCF7L2 perturbation reduces MYC enhancer activity or MYC expression in colorectal cells.
falsified_if: TCF7L2 does not occupy the variant-containing element allele-specifically in colorectal cells.
The ref G allele does not increase TCF7L2 occupancy or MYC enhancer activity.
TCF7L2 perturbation does not change MYC expression or the enhancer reporter.

chains.title: GFI1 binds the ref G allele at the pELS and may repress POU5F1B

links.claim: GFI1 has its own QBiC-SELEX model in group G071 and passes with the same sign as the best model (GFI1 z -29.52), meaning the alt T allele binds less and the ref G allele binds more; GFI1 is expressed at 2.9 TPM in the supplied HCT116 context. This is an in vitro binding prediction, not allele-specific ChIP evidence.
rs6983267 lies in the proximal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3858447.

POU5F1B is the nearest protein-coding gene and has the strongest supplied L2G score; the alt T allele is associated with higher POU5F1B expression in Colon-Transverse, but no evidence directly links GFI1 occupancy at this enhancer to POU5F1B regulation.
GFI1 is expressed at 2.9 TPM in the supplied HCT116 expression context, making this chain testable in colorectal cancer cells.
The variant is associated with colorectal cancer and colon phenotypes, but effect alleles are mixed across traits and the GFI1-dependent direction is not established.

predictions: The ref G allele shows stronger GFI1 binding than the alt T allele.
GFI1 occupancy at the enhancer is detectable in colorectal cells and GFI1 perturbation changes POU5F1B expression.
If GFI1 represses, the ref G allele gives lower enhancer output and the alt T allele gives higher POU5F1B.
falsified_if: GFI1 does not bind the variant allele-specifically.
The ref G allele does not increase GFI1 occupancy.
GFI1 perturbation has no effect on POU5F1B expression or the enhancer reporter.

grades_v0.reason: The binding link is entirely unsupported: no TCF7L2 QBiC result, ChIP peak, allele-specific assay, or perturbation is cited. The element and phenotype links are supported, but the gene and cell-type links are only indirect. The chain also has direction ambiguity because the strongest CRC GWAS row lists effect allele T, whereas H1 proposes ref G as the TCF7L2-binding/MYC-raising allele.

E01 identifies the variant as an enhancer-region noncoding variant and E03 places it in cCRE EH38E3858447 pELS with DNase/H3K27ac signal. These data support the element annotation, though biosample-specific values are not in the call.

E02 gives MYC at 334.4 kb upstream, and E03 lists nearby genes but not MYC. This makes MYC a plausible 8q24 candidate but does not establish enhancer-MYC contact or regulation; there is no 3D contact, reporter, CRISPR, or allele-specific assay.

E07 establishes the supplied DepMap context ACH-000971, but it does not quantify TCF7L2 expression or prove HCT116 is the relevant colorectal model for TCF7L2. The claim is appropriately cautious but only indirectly supported.

E04 and E06a strongly support a CRC association at 8q24.21. However, the strongest CRC row reports effect allele T, while several colon-phenotype rows report G, so allele direction must be reconciled with H1's ref-G binding claim.

E08 supports HNF4A having an own model in group G372 and expression at 2.95 TPM, and the group's passing model predicts alt T binds more. But the passing allelic model is NR2E1, not HNF4A; no HNF4A-specific allelic z-score is shown. This is a QBiC prediction inferred through shared group specificity, so it is at best weak and not allele-specific evidence for HNF4A.
E01 and E03 support that rs6983267 lies in an active enhancer-like pELS. The element identity itself is supported.

E02, E05, E06b, E06c and E06d prioritize POU5F1B (nearest protein-coding gene, strongest L2G, TWAS candidate, CRC biology). They do not show that this enhancer regulates POU5F1B; no chromatin contact, CRISPR perturbation, or allele-specific reporter links the element to POU5F1B.
E08 directly reports HNF4A expression at 2.95 TPM in the supplied HCT116 context, supporting the cell-type expression premise.

E04 and E06a support the CRC association. The strongest CRC row lists effect allele T, which is at least directionally consistent with H2's alt-T-binding allele, but other colon rows list G, so the phenotype effect allele is mixed.

E10 shows GFI1 as a passing member of group G071 with z -29.52 and the same alt-less/ref-more sign as the GFI1B best model, and GFI1 has an own model. This is still only a QBiC-SELEX binding prediction, with no ChIP or allele-specific assay.
E03 supports the pELS element annotation containing the variant.

E02 and E05 support POU5F1B as nearest and top L2G candidate, but no evidence links GFI1 occupancy at this enhancer to POU5F1B regulation. The chain title's 'represses' is not supported by any cited perturbation or reporter data.
E10 reports GFI1 at 2.9 TPM in the supplied HCT116 context, directly supporting expression in the chosen cell type.

E04 supports the CRC/colon association, but effect alleles are mixed. If GFI1 represses an oncogenic POU5F1B, the ref-G-binding claim could run opposite to G-risk colon signals; direction is not resolved.
E12 shows ZBTB43 as the passing own model in group G404 with z -23.26 and effect -1.724, meaning ref binds more. This supports only a QBiC-SELEX prediction, not physical allele-specific binding.
E03 supports the pELS element annotation containing the variant.
E02 and E05 support POU5F1B as nearest and top L2G candidate, but there is no evidence connecting ZBTB43 occupancy at this enhancer to POU5F1B or any other 8q24 target.
E12 reports ZBTB43 at 8.32 TPM in the supplied HCT116 context, directly supporting expression in the chosen cell type.
E04 supports the CRC/colon association, but allele direction is heterogeneous across traits and no ZBTB43-specific effect direction is established.

checks.why: H1 currently has no TCF7L2 evidence at all; an ENCODE ChIP-seq peak containing the variant in colorectal cells would at least support occupancy, though not allele specificity.
H2 infers HNF4A allele direction from an NR2E1 model in group G372; a direct HNF4A lookup would show whether HNF4A has its own/mapped passing model and what direction it predicts.
This would test whether the variant is associated with expression of the proposed target genes in colon tissue, moving beyond nearest-gene/L2G/TWAS prioritization.

In the post-GWAS analyses, we first identified new genome-wide significant associations: three genomic risk loci were identified at 8q24.21 (rs6983267, P = 6.98 × 10-12), 15q13.3 (rs58658771, P = 1.40 × 10-10), and 18q21.1 (rs6507874, P = 1.91 × 10-14).

In addition, the TWAS also identified four loci statistically significantly associated with CRC risk, largely explained by expression regulation, including six candidate genes (DUSP10, POU5F1B, C11orf53, COLCA1, COLCA2, and GREM1-AS1).

Here, upon characterizing cancer-specific transposable element-driven transpochimeric gene transcripts (TcGTs) produced by this tumor in the SYSCOL cohort, we find that expression of the hominid-restricted retrogene POU5F1B through aberrant activation of a primate-specific endogenous retroviral promoter is a strong negative prognostic biomarker.
Correlating this observation, we demonstrate that POU5F1B fosters the proliferation and metastatic potential of CRC cells.
